classification.difficultyReason: The student sets up similar triangles from the supplied diagram and solves for s in terms of x. They differentiate to get ds/dt, then reinterpret the tip as x+s for part b. The model must be built, but the diagram helps.

content.prompt: A streetlight is on top of a 7.5 metre pole. A child $1.8\text{ m}$ tall walks away from the pole at $1.5\text{ m/s}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the length of the shadow is changing.

answer.worked:
Let $s$ be the shadow length and $x$ the distance between the child and the pole. Using similar triangles,
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{s}{s+x}&=\frac{1.8}{7.5}\\7.5s&=1.8s+1.8x\\5.7s&=1.8x\\s&=\frac{6x}{19}\\\frac{ds}{dx}&=\frac{6}{19}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{ds}{dt}&=\frac{ds}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=\frac{6}{19}(1.5)\\&=\frac{9}{19}\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the rate at which the tip of the shadow is moving away from the pole.

answer.worked:
Let $D=x+s$ be the distance from the pole to the tip of the shadow. Using similar triangles,
$$\begin{aligned}s&=\frac{6x}{19}\\D&=x+\frac{6x}{19}\\D&=\frac{25x}{19}\\\frac{dD}{dx}&=\frac{25}{19}.\end{aligned}$$
Hence
$$\begin{aligned}\frac{dD}{dt}&=\frac{dD}{dx}\frac{dx}{dt}\\&=\frac{25}{19}(1.5)\\&=\frac{75}{38}\text{ m/s}.\end{aligned}$$
